metadata.note: The Upper Coos Railroad (North Stratford – Colebrook – Beecher Falls, opened 1887-88) and its operation by the Maine Central from the 1 May 1890 lease as the Beecher Falls Branch: the MEC's own 1891 extension Quebec Junction – Lancaster – North Stratford (Vermont bank), the 1949 trackage-rights reroute via Groveton over the B&M and Grand Trunk, and the leased Hereford Railway in Quebec (Beecher Falls – Lime Ridge). North Stratford – Colebrook is split at the 1 May 1890 lease into two features on identical geometry (Rule 4). The 1933-1955 B&M control of the MEC was through the board and did not change who ran the trains — not a split.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing drawn after passenger service. Not drawn: MEC freight on North Stratford – Beecher Falls after the last confirmed passenger year (to the final MEC run 17 Feb 1977), the North Stratford Railroad Corp. freight 1977 – 1989 embargo, the Beecher Falls furniture-plant traffic, MEC freight on Waumbek Jct – Quebec Jct to its 1976 abandonment, and the Hereford Railway remnant beyond Malvina after 1925.
metadata.line_label_audit: Labels written to Rule 6 at creation.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN END: last passenger (mixed) train North Stratford – Beecher Falls (maine-central-beecher-falls-branch) and Lancaster – North Stratford via Groveton — confirmed to 1954 (Fowler d, MEC public timetable); MEC passenger service ended system-wide Sept 1960 and the Mountain Division's on 26 Apr 1958. Leads: Ron Johnson, 'Maine Central Railroad Mountain Division' (470 Railroad Club, 1986); an NH PUC / ICC discontinuance record; the Colebrook News and Sentinel 1954-1960.

OPEN END: Quebec Junction – North Stratford via the Vermont bank confirmed only to 1932; Quebec Jct – Lancaster ended between 1932 and 1954, Lancaster – North Stratford (Vermont bank) between 1932 and 1948/49. If the 1927/29/33/38 MEC 'Time Table No.' tables are shown to list passenger trains, this could be drawn to 1938.
OPEN END: Hereford Railway (Beecher Falls – Lime Ridge) confirmed to 1921; the last MEC passenger train was between 1921 and the 1925 lease cancellation.

properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: no running time was read from a timetable. ~30 km/h assumes a lightly built single-track steam branch worked in its later decades by a mixed train; not sourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator=MEC (railway=rail/disused/abandoned; incl. the 'Presidential Rail Trail', 'New Hampshire Central Railroad' and 'Upper Coos Recreational Rail Trail' ways) fetched from the mail.ru Overpass mirror 2026-10-15 with opstrace.fetch_operator_ways, routed by opstrace.trace, Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the same boxes and has no railway ways here. Identical sub-path (first 84 vertices) of maine-central-beecher-falls-branch, cut at the vertex nearest the Colebrook town node (Nominatim 'Colebrook, New Hampshire', 498 m away).
properties.geometry_quality: Fully traced on the branch's own OSM-mapped alignment (old_railway_operator=MEC: live 'New Hampshire Central Railroad' track north of North Stratford, then the abandoned grade/rail-trail); no straight-line legs. Traced 12.8 mi North Stratford – Colebrook; no documented North Stratford – Colebrook mileage was in the research report (the whole branch is 22.5 mi, North Stratford MP 130.9 – Beecher Falls MP 153.4, Fowler). The Colebrook end is the line's closest point to the town centre, not a pinned depot site. Era: the alignment drawn is the one the Maine Central later operated; no evidence of a different 1887-90 alignment was found.

segments.note: Upper Coos Railroad (George Van Dyke's logging-promoter road), steam from opening. 'Formally opened from North Stratford to Colebrook, November 29, 1887' (History of the town of Stratford, 1925, pp. 235-236, citing the Coös County History p. 137). Ends at this operator's last day, 30 Apr 1890: leased to and operated by the Maine Central from 1 May 1890 (ICC valuation report, Maine Central Railroad Co., 1931, via nashuacitystation.org; the town history gives the same date) — service continued, see maine-central-beecher-falls-branch. The stop at MP 134.6 appears as 'Eaton's Siding' in the Feb 1889 Pathfinder (Fowler). Operator: treated as the Upper Coos itself (its own superintendent, James Twohey, per the town history); no source says in terms that the Grand Trunk did not work it. Colebrook – Beecher Falls (completed c.1888 per Wikipedia only) is deliberately NOT drawn for this pre-lease era. headway_min 720 (about two trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE; no 1887-90 timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: opening 29 Nov 1887 from the 1925 History of the town of Stratford pp. 235-236; end = Maine Central lease effective 1 May 1890 (ICC 1931 valuation report as transcribed at nashuacitystation.org); Feb 1889 Pathfinder listing of Eaton's Siding via Fowler. Operator identity and headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Fully traced on the branch's own OSM-mapped alignment; no straight-line legs. Traced 22.5 mi North Stratford – Beecher Falls against 22.5 mi documented (Fowler, MEC line 2: North Stratford MP 130.9, Beecher Falls MP 153.4). North Stratford – about Columbia is still track (OSM 'New Hampshire Central Railroad'); the rest is the abandoned grade / Upper Coos Recreational Rail Trail. The North Stratford – Colebrook part is shared vertex-for-vertex with upper-coos-north-stratford-colebrook. Era: the drawn alignment is the line's only known alignment.

segments.note: Maine Central under lease of the Upper Coos Railroad from 1 May 1890 (ICC 1931 valuation report via nashuacitystation.org; 1925 Stratford town history). Positively in the MEC PUBLIC timetable at every Fowler snapshot — 1892/94, 1911, 1921, 1932 and 1954 (Fowler, New Hampshire Railroads, MEC line 2, letters z-d on Colebrook, West Stewartstown, Beecher Falls; North Stratford is not lettered 1911). In its last decades a MIXED train (Dwight Smith, 'Beecher Falls Milk': 'the Beecher Falls mixed', early 1950s, connecting at Quebec Junction with Mountain Division #163); mixed trains carrying passengers count. Passenger service confirmed to 1954 by the 1954 MEC public timetable (Fowler letter d). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end — no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Bounds: the Mountain Division's own last passenger trains ran 26 Apr 1958 and the MEC ran no passenger trains anywhere after Sept 1960. Freight continued (MEC to 17 Feb 1977; then the North Stratford Railroad to a 1989 embargo) — context only, not drawn. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: start = lease date 1 May 1890 (ICC 1931 via nashuacitystation.org; 1925 Stratford town history); service confirmed in MEC public timetables 1892/94, 1911, 1921, 1932, 1954 (Fowler, MEC line 2); mixed-train character early 1950s (Dwight Smith). End year is the last confirmed year [OPEN]. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Maine Central: Quebec Junction – North Stratford (via Guildhall)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: no running time was read from a timetable. ~30 km/h assumes a lightly built single-track steam branch worked in its later decades by a mixed train; not sourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator=MEC (railway=rail/disused/abandoned; incl. the 'Presidential Rail Trail', 'New Hampshire Central Railroad' and 'Upper Coos Recreational Rail Trail' ways) fetched from the mail.ru Overpass mirror 2026-10-15 with opstrace.fetch_operator_ways, routed by opstrace.trace, Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the same boxes and has no railway ways here. Quebec Junction is pinned at the junction node of the MEC Mountain Division and the branch (44.3478,-71.5525); intermediate waypoints Guildhall and Maidstone were pinned ON the MEC grade (Nominatim returned town centroids), not at station sites. One synthetic two-point chord bridges an unmapped gap in the grade near Guildhall.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced on the MEC's own OSM-mapped alignment except as named. Quebec Junction – Lancaster: 12.2 mi traced vs 11.9 mi documented (Fowler MP 98.4 – 110.3), all on MEC-tagged ways (Quebec Jct – Waumbek Jct on the MEC-tagged disused track and Presidential Rail Trail, then MEC-tagged track to Lancaster). Lancaster – North Stratford (Vermont bank, via Coos Junction, Guildhall, Maidstone): 20.3 mi traced vs 20.6 mi documented (Fowler MP 110.3 – 130.9), 19.6 mi on MEC-tagged abandoned grade, ~0.3 mi untagged/connector joins, and ONE APPROXIMATED STRAIGHT-LINE LEG of 0.4 mi (44.5641,-71.5942 to 44.5678,-71.5889, near Guildhall) where OSM has no mapped grade. Total 32.5 mi vs 32.5 mi documented. Era: this is the ORIGINAL 1891 MEC alignment, including the Vermont-bank track removed 1948/49 — correct for the drawn 1891-1932 span; it is NOT the post-1949 route (see maine-central-lancaster-north-stratford-via-groveton).

segments.note: Built and always operated by the Maine Central after the 1890 lease: 'Trains began to run from Quebec Junction to North Stratford, February, 1891' (1925 Stratford town history p. 235; Wikipedia agrees on 1891). In the MEC public timetable 1892/94 (Fowler z on Riverton, Lancaster, Guildhall, Maidstone, Mason's, North Stratford) through 1932 (Fowler c on Waumbek Jct, Bailey's, Riverton, Lancaster, Guildhall, Stevens, Maidstone, Mason's). Passenger service confirmed to 1932 by the 1932 MEC public timetable. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end — no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Brackets: Quebec Jct – Lancaster lost passengers between 1932 and 1954 (in 1954 Lancaster is the TERMINUS, Fowler 'd(tm)', yet Dwight Smith has the early-1950s mixed reaching Quebec Junction); Lancaster – North Stratford on this Vermont-bank alignment ended between 1932 and 1948/49, when the MEC moved to trackage rights via Groveton and its own track was removed. The 1927/29/33/38 MEC 'Time Table No.' tables (nashuacitystation.org) may be employee timetables and are not used to extend this. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: start Feb 1891 from the 1925 Stratford town history p. 235; service confirmed in MEC public timetables 1892/94-1932 (Fowler, MEC line 2). End year is the last confirmed year [OPEN]. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Maine Central: Lancaster – North Stratford (via Groveton)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: no running time was read from a timetable. ~30 km/h assumes a lightly built single-track steam branch worked in its later decades by a mixed train; not sourced.
properties.geometry_source: MEC-tagged track Lancaster – Coos Junction (first two vertices, shared with maine-central-quebec-junction-north-stratford), then OpenStreetMap ways of OTHER COMPANIES' track: old_railway_operator=B&M (Groveton Branch, still rail) Coos Junction – Groveton and old_railway_operator=CN / operator St. Lawrence and Atlantic (Berlin Subdivision, the former Grand Trunk) Groveton – North Stratford, routed by opstrace.trace (mail.ru Overpass mirror, 2026-10-15), DP 8 m + trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced on existing rail throughout; no straight-line legs, except a 202 m join at Coos Junction between the MEC and B&M ways, which share no OSM node there. Traced 21.7 mi Lancaster – North Stratford; no documented mileage for this routing was found (research report: ~20 mi, NOT SOURCED). This is the B&M's and Grand Trunk's track, which the Maine Central used by trackage rights; the B&M/GT have their own features on it elsewhere in data/. Era: current track on the 1949-era alignment; no change known.

segments.note: Maine Central branch train (a mixed) over Boston & Maine (Berlin Branch / Groveton Branch, Coos Junction – Groveton) and Grand Trunk/Canadian National (Groveton – North Stratford) rails by trackage rights, which replaced the MEC's own Vermont-bank track. SOURCE CONFLICT on the start: 1949 (nekrailroad.com) vs 1948 (Wikipedia); the later year is drawn. In the 1954 MEC public timetable (Fowler letter d on Coos Junction and North Stratford; Lancaster 'd(tm)', i.e. the 1954 train terminated at Lancaster). Passenger service confirmed to 1954 by that timetable. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end — no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Ceiling: MEC ran no passenger trains after Sept 1960. Dwight Smith's Sunday 'Maine Central extra from Colebrook to Lancaster' (milk for a B&M Lancaster – Woodsville train) fits this routing. headway_min 1440 (one round trip a day) is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: trackage-rights start from nekrailroad.com (1949; Wikipedia says 1948 — conflict recorded); 1954 service from Fowler, MEC line 2 (letter d). End year is the last confirmed year [OPEN]. Headway and mileage not sourced.

properties.line: Maine Central: Hereford Railway (Beecher Falls – Lime Ridge)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: no running time was read from a timetable. ~30 km/h assumes a lightly built single-track steam branch worked in its later decades by a mixed train; not sourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator='Maine Central Railway' (name 'Beecher Falls Branch', 'Chemin du Maine Central', 'Chemin de l'Ancien-Maine', etc.) (railway=rail/disused/abandoned; incl. the 'Presidential Rail Trail', 'New Hampshire Central Railroad' and 'Upper Coos Recreational Rail Trail' ways) fetched from the mail.ru Overpass mirror 2026-10-15 with opstrace.fetch_operator_ways, routed by opstrace.trace, Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the same boxes and has no railway ways here. Quebec waypoints were geocoded by hand with Nominatim (countrycodes=ca) and pinned; Cookshire and Dudswell Junction were pinned on the grade.
properties.geometry_quality: Fully traced on the Hereford Railway's own OSM-mapped grade; no straight-line legs. Traced 53.0 mi Beecher Falls – Lime Ridge against 53.1 mi documented (Fowler, Quebec MEC line 93: MP 153.4 – 206.5). 52.4 mi on 'Maine Central Railway'-tagged ways, ~0.3 mi untagged join across the border at Beecher Falls/Hereford, 0.2 mi on a way tagged 'Quebec Central Railway' but named 'Beecher Falls Branch' near Dudswell Junction. Lies in southern Quebec except ~0.6 mi in Vermont; inside the map bounds (CLAUDE.md Rule 9 southern-Canada allowance for a US railroad). Era: the line's only alignment.

segments.note: Hereford Railway, leased to and operated by the Maine Central from 1 May 1890 (1925 Stratford town history: 'also leased to the Maine Central ... from May 1, 1890'; a 990-year lease). Drawn from the first confirmation, the 1894 Pathfinder (Fowler, Quebec MEC line 93, letter z on Hereford, Malvina, St. Malo, Sawyerville, Cookshire Jct, Dudswell Jct, 'Lime Ridge-Marbleton' and others); the line was built 1889-90 (Wikipedia) but 1890-93 passenger service is not confirmed and is not drawn. In the MEC public timetables of 1911 and 1921 (Fowler a, b); the 1919 USRA MEC timetable (nashuacitystation.org) still carries 'Quebec Junction to Lime Ridge'. Passenger service confirmed to 1921 by the 1921 MEC public timetable. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end — no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Ceiling: the MEC cancelled the lease in 1925 and border – Malvina track was removed (Wikipedia); the 1927 MEC table ends at Beecher Falls. Later operation of the remnant beyond Malvina is not drawn. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: lease 1 May 1890 from the 1925 Stratford town history p. 235; service confirmed 1894 (Pathfinder), 1911 and 1921 (MEC public timetables) via Fowler, Quebec MEC line 93; 1919 USRA timetable via nashuacitystation.org. End year is the last confirmed year [OPEN]. Headway not sourced.
